newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-DRAKES TAKES EIGHT WICKETS AGAINST NATAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DRAKES TAKES EIGHT WICKETS AGAINST NATAL.

text.p: West Indian fast bowler Vasbert Drakes announced himself as an overseas signing of worth at Kingsmead on Saturday when he finished with an impressive return of 8-59 for Border against Natal.

Having taken three wickets on the first day, Drakes ripped through the Natal lower order for the home side to be bowled out for 332 in their first innings before lunch on the second day of their four-day Supersport Series cricket match.
The 26-year-old Barbadian took five wickets for just seven runs in the morning as Natal could add only 17 runs to their overnight total of 315.
"The ball wasn't swinging and I was just looking to cut down my pace, cramp the batsmen up a bit and make it difficult for them to score," Drakes told Reuters.
"(Dale) Benkenstein and (Shaun) Pollock had been batting pretty well and initially we aimed to bowl an accurate line and length to contain them in the morning. It's a pretty decent batting wicket."
Drakes' figures of 30.3-8-59-8 could well be the best in the competition by the end of the 1996-97 season.
Yet Drakes, who represented the West Indies in five one-day internationals against Australia during 1995, has a better haul of first-class wickets to his credit.
"I took 8-48 against Guyana in the Red Stripe competition in 1994 and that side included the likes of test players Shivnareen Chanderpaul and Carl Hooper.

"In some ways, I wish Andrew Hudson and Jonty Rhodes had been playing for Natal in this match because you always want to play against the best. But then again, they might have got a few Drakes, who was recommended to Border by fellow West Indians Ottis Gibson and Cammie Smith, can expect to bowl a lot of overs for his new province this season. However his captain Pieter Strydom would be well advised to employ him as the spearhead of the attack, rather than as the brunt.
An athletic fast bowler with a languid approach to the wicket, Drakes generally angles the ball into the right-handed batsman and he has an intelligent of pace.

He sees himself as a thinking bowler: "I can bowl pretty quick and can also swing the ball but that depends on the conditions. Generally, I prefer to cut my pace down and try to work the batsman out."
Understudy to Franklyn Stephenson as overseas player for English county Sussex for three years, Drakes played his first full season based at Hove earlier this year.
He took 50 first-class wickets for Sussex at an average of 33.5 but he believes his tie playing domestic cricket in South Africa will be of more benefit.
"Malcolm Marshall told me it's the most competitive first-class cricket you can get -- and that's the beauty of it over here."
On the evidence of his bowling in his first-class debut for Border, it is clear Drakes can also teach South African cricket something.
